company.name: D.R. Horton, Inc.
company.does: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States with operations in 126 markets across 36 states. D.R. Horton mainly builds single-family homes (over 90% of home sales revenue) and offers products to entry-level, move-up, luxury buyers, and active adults. The company offers homebuyers mortgage financing and title agency services through its financial services segment. The firm has majority ownership of Forestar Group, a publicly traded residential lot development company. D.R. Horton's headquarters are in Arlington, Texas.

company.name: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.
company.does: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd is an asset-light container liner shipping company. It offers tailored services, including land transportation and logistical services, specialized shipping solutions, including the transportation of out-of-gauge cargo, refrigerated cargo, and dangerous and hazardous cargo. Its services include Cargo Services, Digital Services, Schedules, and Shipping Trades and Lines. Geographically, it derives a majority of its revenue from the Pacific trade region.

company.name: Vistra Corp.
company.does: Vistra Corp. is one of the largest power producers and retail energy providers in the US. It owns 44 gigawatts of generation capacity, including natural gas (27 GW), nuclear (6.5 GW), coal (8.7 GW), and solar and battery storage (1.3 GW). The Cogentrix acquisition will add 5.5 GW of gas generation. Vistra's retail electricity business serves 5 million customers in 20 states, including almost a third of all Texas electricity consumers. Vistra emerged from the Energy Future Holdings bankruptcy as a stand-alone entity in 2016.

company.name: First Solar, Inc.
company.does: First Solar designs and manufactures solar photovoltaic panels, modules, and systems primarily for use in utility-scale projects. Its modules use cadmium telluride, rather than the crystalline silicon used by most of the industry to convert sunlight into electricity. The technology does not rely on Chinese crystalline silicon supply chains. Its primary manufacturing is in the US. It has additional factories in India, Malaysia, and Vietnam. Its primary markets are the US and India.

company.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
company.does: With roughly one-third of the global branded diabetes treatment market, Novo Nordisk is the world's leading provider of diabetes care products. Based in Denmark, the company manufactures and markets a variety of human and modern insulins for patients with diabetes, as well as injectable and oral GLP-1 therapies, across its obesity and diabetes care segment. Novo also has a rare disease segment (contributing less than 10% of revenue) that specializes in protein therapies for hemophilia and other disorders.

company.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
company.does: Founded in 1937, Toyota is one of the world's largest automakers, with 11.3 million units sold at retail in fiscal 2026, including 10.5 million across the Toyota and Lexus brands. Brands include Toyota, Lexus, Daihatsu, and truck maker Hino; market share in Japan is about 51% excluding minivehicles, while US share is around 15%. The firm also owns stakes in Denso, a parts supplier, about 20% of Subaru, and holds investments in many other firms, including shares of Uber Technologies, Joby Aviation, Aurora Innovation, Isuzu Motors, and about 5% in each of Mazda and Suzuki. Fiscal 2026 sales excluding financial services were JPY 46.1 trillion. Toyota also has a financing arm and manufactures homes and boats.

company.name: Chubb Limited
company.does: ACE acquired Chubb in 2016 and assumed the Chubb name. The combination made the new Chubb one of the largest domestic property and casualty insurers, with operations in over 50 countries spanning commercial and personal P&C insurance, reinsurance, and life insurance.

news.title: Prediction: $10,000 Invested in Viking Therapeutics Before Its Oral Phase 3 Readouts Could Be Worth This Much by 2028
news.summary: Viking Therapeutics is conducting phase 3 trials for its obesity drug VK2735 in both injectable and oral forms. The oral formulation could expand the addressable market through a dual-dosing strategy. With conservative assumptions of 50% phase 3 success rate and 10% market share of tirzepatide's peak sales, Viking's stock could reach $110 per share by 2028, making a $10,000 investment worth up to $47,800.

news.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights First Solar, Sunrun and Tigo Energy
news.summary: The U.S. solar industry faces headwinds from rising interest rates, shifting trade policies, and tariffs that could increase equipment costs and delay projects. However, strong demand from data centers, corporate decarbonization commitments, and battery storage adoption support long-term growth. The solar industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank #150 (bottom 39%), reflecting negative earnings revisions. Three companies highlighted are Sunrun (Rank #2 Buy), First Solar (Rank #3 Hold), and Tigo Energy (Rank #3).

news.title: Forget Buying All 7 "Magnificent Seven" Stocks. Here's How to Rank 6 Top AI Stocks Right Now (Hint: It Has to Do With Anthropic.)
news.summary: With Anthropic's IPO expected to price on November 18, 2026, the article ranks six AI and infrastructure stocks by their direct exposure to Anthropic's spending. Amazon and Alphabet have the most direct ties as investors and suppliers, while Nvidia has moderate exposure. Energy companies like Bloom Energy, Vistra, and Oklo offer indirect exposure through data center power needs.

news.title: Can LLY's Expanding Obesity Pipeline Sustain Its GLP-1 Leadership?
news.summary: Eli Lilly has established itself as a dominant player in the obesity treatment market, with Mounjaro and Zepbound generating 65% of revenues. The company's April 2026 launch of Foundayo (oral GLP-1) recorded $281 million in sales, offering a more convenient alternative to injectable treatments. Lilly is developing next-generation therapies including retatrutide (triple-acting), eloralintide, and EloraTZP to maintain market leadership. However, competition is intensifying from Novo Nordisk and emerging biotech companies.

news.title: 3 Solar Stocks to Watch Amid Policy and Interest Rate Headwinds
news.summary: The U.S. solar market is expected to double between 2026 and 2031, driven by rising electricity demand, corporate decarbonization commitments, and data center expansion. However, the industry faces significant challenges from shifting trade policies including tariffs and import restrictions that could increase equipment costs and disrupt supply chains, as well as elevated interest rates that increase financing costs for solar projects. The Zacks Solar industry currently ranks in the bottom 39% of industries with negative earnings revisions.

news.title: AI in Drug Discovery Market to Reach USD 15,536.2 Million by 2033 at 25.1% CAGR | Coherent Market Insights
news.summary: The global AI in drug discovery market is projected to grow from USD 3,240.0 million in 2026 to USD 15,536.2 million by 2033, with a CAGR of 25.1%. Growth is driven by increasing pharmaceutical investments in AI infrastructure, machine learning adoption, and collaborations between pharma companies and AI providers. North America leads with 51.6% market share, while Asia Pacific shows the fastest growth at 27.2% CAGR. Key trends include generative AI for molecule design, multimodal AI for biological data analysis, and growing focus on AI model validation.

news.title: Bull of the Day: International Seaways (INSW)
news.summary: International Seaways (INSW), a major tanker operator, has surged over 100% year-to-date driven by booming tanker demand and elevated charter rates. The company posted exceptional Q3 results with 146% revenue growth and 408% earnings growth. With a Zacks Rank #1 rating, attractive 6X forward P/E valuation, and a 20%+ dividend yield, analysts project FY26-27 EPS will be 375% above prior year levels, suggesting further upside despite the spectacular rally.

news.title: JPMorgan Predicted Strong Wegovy Pill Sales (and Was Right). Is Novo Nordisk Stock a Buy Now?
news.summary: Novo Nordisk exceeded JPMorgan's expectations with strong Wegovy pill sales, accumulating over 8 million prescriptions. However, the company is in a transition phase toward a high-volume/low-price model, causing operating profit to fall 9% year-over-year. While the stock has fallen 70% from its 2024 peak and offers an attractive 4.4% dividend yield, investors should weigh the company's strategic shift against competition from Eli Lilly and other GLP-1 drug makers.

news.title: Vistra Corp. (VST) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.summary: Vistra Corp. (VST) has attracted investor attention despite a -19.2% decline over the past month, significantly underperforming its industry. The company shows strong revenue growth projections (+23.3% for current fiscal year) and substantial earnings growth (+65.2% for current fiscal year), but recent earnings estimate revisions have been slightly negative. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and a B valuation grade indicating the stock trades at a discount to peers, the company is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.title: Investors Heavily Search Chubb Limited (CB): Here is What You Need to Know
news.summary: Chubb Limited (CB) has gained 6.6% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's -3.7% decline. The insurer has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with consensus earnings estimates showing +16.5% year-over-year growth for the current fiscal year. The company has consistently beaten EPS estimates in the trailing four quarters and trades at a valuation discount to peers (Value Grade B), suggesting it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.title: Why Chubb (CB) is a Top Momentum Stock for the Long-Term
news.summary: Zacks Premium offers investment research tools including the Zacks Rank and Style Scores to help investors identify high-performing stocks. The platform features daily updates, equity research reports, and premium stock screens. Chubb Limited (CB) is highlighted as a stock to watch with a #3 Hold rank and strong Momentum Style Score of A, with shares up 6.6% over four weeks and upward earnings revisions.

news.title: GLP-1 RAs & Incretin-based Therapies Competitive Landscape Analysis: Key Developments by 200+ Companies Shaping the Treatment Landscape | DelveInsight
news.summary: DelveInsight released a comprehensive competitive landscape report on GLP-1 receptor agonists and incretin-based therapies, covering 200+ pipeline drugs from 180+ active players. The report highlights approved drugs like MOUNJARO (tirzepatide) and OZEMPIC (semaglutide), with 30+ therapies in late-stage development and 60+ in mid/early stages. Key indications include obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular outcomes. Recent developments include positive Phase III results for retatrutide, survodutide, and other dual/triple agonists from major pharmaceutical companies.

news.title: Here's What Key Metrics Tell Us About Vistra (VST) Q3 Earnings
news.summary: Vistra Corp. reported Q3 2026 revenue of $6.35 billion, up 27.7% year-over-year, but missed analyst expectations of $7.11 billion. EPS of $3.23 exceeded consensus estimates of $2.94. The company showed mixed performance across segments, with strong results in Texas and West regions but underperformance in retail sales volumes and East region EBITDA. The stock has declined 19.2% over the past month and holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

news.title: VST Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Power Pricing, Revenues Rise Y/Y
news.summary: Vistra Corp. reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.23 per share, beating estimates by 9.86% with an 84.6% year-over-year increase. Revenues reached $6.35 billion, up 27.7% but slightly missing consensus estimates. The company raised 2026 guidance and initiated 2027 outlook, supported by higher energy prices, the Cogentrix acquisition, and strong retail performance. Peer utilities Everergy, FirstEnergy, and IDACORP also reported better-than-expected Q3 results.

news.title: Constellation and Vistra Get the Headlines. These 2 Power Producers Barely Get Mentioned.
news.summary: While Constellation Energy and Vistra dominate headlines, Talen Energy and NRG Energy are lesser-known power producers positioned to benefit from growing AI data center demand. Talen has secured a long-term nuclear power supply agreement with Amazon, while NRG is expanding capacity through natural gas assets and the CPower acquisition. Both companies offer attractive valuations but face execution risks and regulatory scrutiny.

news.title: Are Finance Stocks Lagging  Ames National (ATLO) This Year?
news.summary: Ames National (ATLO) has significantly outperformed the Finance sector with a 49.1% year-to-date return compared to the sector average of 5.5%. The company holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, with analyst consensus estimates for full-year earnings improving 3.3% over the past three months. Chubb (CB) is also highlighted as an outperformer with a 16.5% year-to-date return and a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

news.title: T1 Energy to Release Q3 Earnings: Here's What You Need to Know
news.summary: T1 Energy is set to report Q3 2026 results on November 12, with expectations for higher production and deliveries building on 935 MW output in Q2. The Evervolt acquisition and 641 MW Clearway agreement strengthen the company's technology and demand outlook. However, higher legal, financing, advisory, and workforce costs could pressure profitability. The consensus estimate projects a loss of 12 cents per share with 30.6% revenue growth year-over-year.

news.title: Can CB's Life Insurance Growth Boost Its Wealth Protection Business?
news.summary: Chubb Limited reported 11.4% growth in Life Insurance segment income to $369 million in Q3 2026, driven by international expansion. The company launched new wealth protection products in Indonesia and Bermuda, including the CB Premier Wealth Protection endowment product offering maturity benefits up to 140% of premiums. Chubb also partnered with a neobank in Indonesia to expand distribution. Competitors Manulife and Sun Life are similarly expanding their wealth protection portfolios across Asia.

news.title: Toyota: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.summary: Toyota raised its full-year operating income forecast to JPY 3.9 trillion and announced three strategic initiatives: launching Toyota Robotics as a core business pillar on January 1, building battery-electric vehicles on a foundation of 10 million hybrid vehicles aligned with actual market demand, and targeting JPY 1 trillion in value chain revenue growth by 2030 through maintenance, parts, and financial services.

news.summary: Zacks highlights five stocks with attractive EV-to-EBITDA valuations as bargain opportunities. The article explains why EV-to-EBITDA is a superior valuation metric compared to P/E ratios, particularly for leveraged companies and loss-making firms. Featured stocks include DMC Global, HF Sinclair, Cenovus Energy, ZIM Integrated Shipping, and POSCO, all showing strong expected earnings growth for 2026.

news.title: Can the Blue Wave Save Renewable Energy Stocks?
news.summary: Renewable energy stocks experienced a surge following the November 3 election results, but gave back gains the next day. The article analyzes the performance of major renewable energy companies and discusses what investors should realistically expect from this sector going forward, with Jason Hall highlighting Brookfield Renewable as a top pick.

news.title: Toyota Surges Post Q2 Earnings: Is the Stock Worth Buying Now?
news.summary: Toyota shares rallied over 9% following Q2 fiscal 2027 results, driven by an improved full-year operating profit forecast raised to ¥3.9 trillion and an expanded shareholder return program of ¥1.3 trillion buyback authorization. Despite an 18.5% net income decline, operating profit grew 34%, with strong performance from the automotive division and hybrid sales increasing 8.3%. North America returned to profitability, and management expects hybrid sales to reach 5.01 million units for the full year.

news.title: NMIH Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Higher Claims and Costs
news.summary: NMI Holdings reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.23 per share, missing consensus estimates by 6.8%. While revenues grew 5% year-over-year and the insured portfolio expanded, profitability declined due to surging insurance claims (up 56.9%) and higher underwriting expenses. The combined ratio deteriorated 700 basis points to 38.5%, and net income fell 2.6% year-over-year. The company maintains strong capital reserves and book value growth.

news.title: First Solar, Inc. (FSLR) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.summary: First Solar (FSLR) has gained 9.5% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500. The company shows strong EPS growth expectations of +24.3% for the current fiscal year and +38.9% for next year, though current quarter revenue is expected to decline 12.9% year-over-year. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and a B valuation grade indicating the stock trades at a discount to peers, the company is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.title: Pick These 5 Bargain Stocks With Alluring EV-to-EBITDA Ratios
news.summary: The article explains why EV-to-EBITDA is a superior valuation metric compared to P/E ratios, as it accounts for debt and can value loss-making companies. Five stocks meeting strict screening criteria—DMC Global, HF Sinclair, Cenovus Energy, ZIM Integrated Shipping Services, and POSCO Holdings—are highlighted as undervalued with strong earnings growth projections for 2026.

news.title: Navigator Holdings (NVGS) Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates
news.summary: Navigator Holdings reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.41 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $0.38 but missing revenue expectations at $119.99 million versus the estimated $118.84 million. The stock has outperformed the S&P 500 by 5.3% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The Transportation-Shipping industry ranks in the top 20% of Zacks industries.

news.title: The Best Industrial Stock to Buy With $1,000 Right Now
news.summary: Joby Aviation is recommended as the best industrial stock to buy with $1,000, as it develops electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for urban air taxi services. The company is nearing FAA certification and commercial operations, with backing from Toyota and demonstration flights completed. However, investors should be aware of regulatory risks, high valuation multiples (40x trailing revenue), and the company's path to profitability remains uncertain.

news.title: 5 Stocks Favored by Brokers Amid the Prevalent Market Turbulence
news.summary: Amid elevated oil prices, persistent inflation, and Federal Reserve uncertainty, five broker-favored stocks have emerged as potential investment opportunities. These stocks—Cracker Barrel, ZIM Integrated Shipping, Cleveland-Cliffs, Helen of Troy, and Adient—were selected based on positive earnings estimate revisions and strong broker recommendations, offering investors a strategy to navigate challenging market conditions.

news.title: Harley-Davidson Stock After Q3: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell?
news.summary: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is showing recovery momentum with improved North American retail sales, cost savings initiatives, and strong liquidity, but faces significant headwinds from declining global shipments, rising tariff costs ($105-120M in 2026), weak international demand, and ongoing losses from its LiveWire electric motorcycle division. The company raised 2026 shipment guidance but remains challenged by structural profitability issues.

news.title: D.R. Horton's Q4 Earnings Miss on Weak Housing Demand, Sales Beat
news.summary: D.R. Horton reported Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings of $2.67 per share, missing estimates, while revenues beat expectations at $9.37 billion. The homebuilder faced persistent affordability challenges, rising mortgage rates, and softer demand, with net sales orders declining 7%. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenues of $30-$32 billion with elevated sales incentives expected to continue. Other major homebuilders also reported weaker results amid challenging market conditions.

news.title: PACCAR Stock After Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell?
news.summary: PACCAR benefits from recovering truck demand, strong pricing power, and record aftermarket revenues, but faces headwinds from supply constraints, regulatory uncertainty around 2027 emissions standards, and declining cash flow despite record parts revenues. The company maintains a Hold rating with neutral investor stance recommended until operational challenges ease.

news.title: D.R. Horton (DHI) Misses Q4 Earnings Estimates
news.summary: D.R. Horton reported quarterly earnings of $2.67 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $3.03 per share, representing an 11.88% earnings surprise. While the company exceeded revenue expectations at $9.37 billion, unfavorable estimate revisions ahead of the earnings release resulted in a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating, suggesting underperformance relative to the market. The homebuilder industry ranks in the bottom 5% of Zacks industries.

news.title: What's in Store For These 5 Construction Stocks This Earnings Season?
news.summary: The U.S. construction sector is experiencing divergent trends entering Q3 earnings season. Strong AI and data center investments, along with government infrastructure spending, are boosting public construction demand and benefiting companies like Quanta, EMCOR, and Vulcan. However, elevated mortgage rates (7.28%) and weak consumer sentiment are dampening residential housing demand, pressuring homebuilders like D.R. Horton. Sector earnings are expected to grow 3.4% year-over-year with revenues rising 8.6%, though early reporters have missed estimates.

news.title: D.R. Horton's Q4 Earnings Preview: What Investors Must Know Now?
news.summary: D.R. Horton is expected to report Q4 FY2026 results on Oct. 29 with revenues projected to decline 6.6% year-over-year to $9.04 billion. The homebuilder faces headwinds from elevated mortgage rates, affordability challenges, and increased sales incentives that pressure margins and average selling prices. While lower construction costs may provide some offset, earnings are expected to decline slightly. Backlog value is anticipated to grow despite declining net sales orders.

news.title: D.R. Horton (DHI) Stock Sinks As Market Gains: Here's Why
news.summary: D.R. Horton (DHI) closed down 2.93% and holds a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating. The homebuilder faces declining earnings expectations with Q3 EPS projected to fall 0.33% year-over-year and full-year earnings expected to decline 9.85%. The stock trades at a slight discount to its industry peers with a Forward P/E of 12.24 versus the industry average of 12.43.

content.thinking:
I've got the portfolio sorted, so now I'm turning to what the world looks like in November 2026. The news points to elevated oil prices, stubborn inflation, and uncertainty around the Fed, with mortgage rates sitting high at about 7.28% and the S&P 500 down roughly 3.7% over the past month. I'll also check the November 3 election outcome and the expected timing of Anthropic's IPO.

I'm going through a list of holdings now, noting Vistra's recent drop and its Cogentrix deal, ZIM's possible takeover by Hapag-Lloyd at $35 a share, NVO's steep fall from its peak, and the housing, solar, reinsurance, and Toyota exposures. Before I dig into any of them, I want to check how exposure() is set up and begin with the market factor.

# Dow Rallies 2.9%, Oil Sinks 7% After Midterms: Stock Market Today

Wall Street rallied Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in [Tuesday’s midterm elections](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/26/11/62852177/barack-obama-calls-on-democrats-to-roll-up-their-sleeves-and-prevent-further-damage-after-midterm-election-wins-a-clear-message), putting the Dow Jones Industrial Average on course for its biggest one-day gain in 19 months.

Oil tumbled on bets the result will push Washington toward [an end to the Iran war](https://www.benzinga.com/politics). West Texas Intermediate crude fell 7.2% to \$89.17 a barrel, and Brent sank 8.5% to \$94.84.

Iran’s parliament speaker, **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf**, wrote on X that American voters “said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” while President **Donald Trump** told the Financial Times the U.S. is “locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.”

- The S&P 500 rose 1.8% to 7,701, up 133 points.
- The Dow gained 1,515 points, or 2.9%, to 53,302, its largest one-day advance in both points and percentage terms since April 9, 2025.
- The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.3% to 28,557.
- The Russell 2000 advanced 1.5% to 2,856
- The CBOE Volatility Index dropped 16.7% to 17.35.
- Bonds also rallied: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 6 basis points to 4.90%. The 2-year yield slipped 5 basis points to 4.58%, and the 30-year yield dropped 4 basis points to 5.30%.
- Gold rose 3.3% to \$4,070 an ounce and silver jumped 4.9% to \$52.20.
- **Bitcoin** [(CRYPTO: BTC)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BTC-USD) climbed 4% to \$80,432, back above \$80,000.

On the data front, the ISM services PMI eased to 54.5 in October from 54.9, below the 54.8 forecast, while the prices-paid gauge cooled to 73 from 74. ADP private payrolls rose by 86,000, above the 69,000 forecast.

# Corning to Caterpillar: The AI ‘Picks and Shovels’ Trade Caves In

The industrial companies selling fiber, turbines, cooling systems and grid labor to the AI buildout led the market for most of 2026. But now, they [are leading it lower](https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/analyst-color/26/11/63002288/ai-stocks-got-hammered-after-midterms-but-this-analyst-says-the-panic-is-overblown).

A Democratic sweep of Congress last week turned a slow leak into a rout. The wins included Republican strongholds and the key data center hubs of Texas and Georgia, raising the prospect of greater scrutiny for industries [that benefited from GOP control](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/62918286/top-5-ai-stocks-to-buy-after-midterm-elections-this-strategist-calls-the-sell-off-a-massive-opportunity).

- *GEV stock is moving. [Get all the details here.](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GEV)*

**GE Vernova Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GEV)[GEV](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GEV)) fell 9.3% the day after the elections, while **Constellation Energy Corp.** [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CEG)[CEG](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CEG)) and **Vistra Corp.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST)[VST](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST)), two power producers heavily exposed to Texas data center projects, slid 6.7% and 13.8%. **Vertiv Holdings Co.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VRT)[VRT](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VRT)) dropped 13% the same day on fears of data center moratoriums.\

The damage spread the next session when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.3% on Nov. 5, its worst day since March 2020, and the Nasdaq fell 5.5% to confirm a correction. The Dow lost about 1,800 points.

## The Run-Up Set the Trap

The past 30 days wiped out a big slice of the year’s gains. **Corning Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GLW)[GLW](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GLW)) [fell](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9177208/corning-inc-glw-shares-fall-129-what-gf-score-of-76-tells-investors) 12.9% on Nov. 5 to \$103.43, leaving the stock down 35.1% over the prior month. The fiber maker had a long way to fall. Its shares rose 84% in 2025 on demand from AI data center construction.

Siebert Financial CIO **Mark Malek** framed the changing tide as the industry’s new reality.

"The AI buildout will become more expensive, not disappear," Malek told Reuters. Most analysts doubt legislation could meaningfully stall construction, but a Democratic Congress raises the odds of more hearings, investigations and delays.

**Read Also: [Nvidia Is Now Nearly 3 Times Cheaper Than Intel on Forward Earnings](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/11/63067409/nvidia-is-now-nearly-3-times-cheaper-than-intel-on-forward-earnings)**

**Caterpillar Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAT)[CAT](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAT)) lost 29.7% in the month through Nov. 6, while the S&P 500 fell 4.9%. Earnings day did much of the damage. Shares sank 9.3% on Oct. 29, their worst day since at least the start of 2025, after the company beat third-quarter estimates but held its annual sales forecast, and its record \$78.1 billion backlog missed bullish hopes of \$80 billion.

The rest of the group followed. Vertiv fell 28.3% from Oct. 7 to Nov. 5, and **Eaton Corp. plc** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ETN)[ETN](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ETN)) dropped 24.2% over the same stretch.

GE Vernova slid 15.9% in the month through Nov. 4, and **Quanta Services Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PWR)[PWR](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PWR)) [fell](https://www.trefis.com/stock/vrt/articles/623222/are-you-sure-you-understand-vertiv-stocks-risk/2026-11-06) 14.2% from its Oct. 2 close to Nov. 4.

Buyers finally stepped in on Monday. Corning closed up 9.25% and Caterpillar gained 7.21% on Nov. 9, according to [Benzinga Pro](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3?utm_content=editorial&utm_ad_type=content-text) data.

**GLW, CAT Price Action:** Corning shares were down 1.7% at \$114.00, and Caterpillar shares were down 3% at \$580.64 in early trading Tuesday, according to [Benzinga Pro data](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3).

# ZIM Stock Jumps Nearly 7% Premarket: What's Going On?

Shares of **ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM)[ZIM](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM)) surged nearly 7% in premarket trading on Tuesday following news that [Hapag-Lloyd and private equity fund FIMI](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/07/60281802/why-zim-stock-is-falling-on-hapag-lloyd-merger-update) are revising their \$4.2 billion cash acquisition bid.

## **Addressing Security Concerns**

According to Reuters, the original \$35.00-per-share [all-cash takeover](https://www.benzinga.com/m-a/26/02/50642214/hapag-lloyd-to-buy-zim-for-4-2-billion-in-massive-shipping-deal) encountered strong resistance inside Israel from ZIM workers, Defence Minister **Israel Katz**, and government officials. Opponents claimed the transaction risked national security by handing over critical maritime operations to a foreign enterprise.

Hapag-Lloyd has held several rounds of discussions with Israel’s economy, finance, and defence ministries “to revise structural elements of the proposed acquisition.”

“We are now developing an improved proposal designed to further strengthen Israel’s maritime security and independence,” said Hapag-Lloyd CEO **Rolf Habben Jansen** in a statement. He added that the revised proposal “will secure Israel’s access to key shipping routes, including routes from Asia.”

[Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com) has reached out to ZIM Integrated Shipping Services for comment on the revised acquisition terms and will update this article upon response.

**Read Also: [Stock Market Today: S&P 500, Dow Futures Fall as Oil Tops \$99 Despite Trump’s Price Drop Prediction — ASML, NVS, CASY in Focus](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/09/61651732/stock-market-today-sp-500-dow-futures-fall-as-oil-tops-99-despite-trumps-price-drop-prediction-asml-nvs-casy-in-focus)**

## **Structural Revisions and ‘Golden Share’**

Under the revised deal, Hapag-Lloyd aims to secure its position as the world’s fifth-largest [shipping group](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/05/52701252/zim-integrated-profit-hit-stems-from-shipping-market-weakness), as per the company statement. Meanwhile, FIMI will take ownership of a dedicated company called ZIM Israel, carved out with 16 vessels to secure direct global maritime connections and assume full responsibility for Israel’s “golden share.”

To limit foreign influence, according to Reuters, Hapag-Lloyd proposed lowering the maximum single foreign investor shareholding threshold without government notification from 24% down to 10%. FIMI also committed not to list ZIM Israel’s shares on foreign stock exchanges.

“The agreement will also prevent any foreign interference in the [transportation of](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/03/51137968/zim-stock-climbs-as-market-shrugs-off-weak-freight-rates) Israel’s sensitive cargo, representing a significant improvement over the current arrangement,” Habben Jansen stated.

The revised proposal is scheduled for submission to Israel’s cabinet later this month.

## **How Has ZIM Performed in 2026?**

Price Action: At the last check, the ZIM stock was trading 6.70% higher in premarket trading on Tuesday. It was up 34.62% year-to-date, advancing by 114.40% over the last year, and fell 0.94% over the last six months. It closed 3.59% higher at \$28.58 per share on Friday.

# ZIM Stock Nears 52-Week High As Freight Boom Fuels Massive Profit Outlook Hike

**ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM)[(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM)[ZIM](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM)) stock is trading higher Wednesday after the Israeli container shipping company sharply raised its full-year 2026 outlook, citing strong demand and favorable [freight-rate trends](https://www.benzinga.com/pressreleases/26/10/n62204616/zim-raises-full-year-2026-guidance).

## ZIM Raises 2026 Profit Outlook

ZIM said Tuesday it now expects adjusted EBITDA of between \$2.7 billion and \$3 billion for 2026. That compares with its previous forecast of \$2 billion to \$2.4 billion.

The company also raised its adjusted EBIT forecast to between \$1.4 billion and \$1.7 billion. Its previous outlook called for \$700 million to \$1.1 billion.

At the midpoint, the new guidance represents a 30% increase in expected adjusted EBITDA and a 72% jump in adjusted EBIT from the outlook ZIM issued on Aug. 19.

The company attributed the stronger forecast to continued robust market demand and favorable momentum in freight rates.

Higher container freight rates can have an outsized impact on shipping companies because much of their vessel and operating cost base is fixed or contracted. Stronger rates can therefore translate quickly into higher operating profit when demand remains firm.

**See More: [Top Value Stocks](https://www.benzinga.com/screener/top-value-stocks)**

## Hapag-Lloyd Deal Remains In Focus

The stronger operating outlook comes as investors continue to monitor ZIM’s pending acquisition by **Hapag-Lloyd AG**.

Hapag-Lloyd agreed to acquire ZIM in a roughly \$4.2 billion transaction valued [at \$35 per share](https://www.benzinga.com/node/50642214).

However, the deal still faces a regulatory hurdle in Israel.

The Israeli Government Companies Authority stopped processing the parties’ existing [approval](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1654126/000117891326004656/zk2636172.htm) application after Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI failed to submit a detailed revised proposal for ZIM’s post-closing operations by the regulator’s deadline.

The authority said any new proposal concerning the merger or Israel’s special state share in ZIM must be submitted in full detail for review. Hapag-Lloyd has told ZIM that it intends to submit a revised proposal and again seek approval from Israeli authorities.

ZIM’s regulatory disclosures also identify the pending Hapag-Lloyd transaction, geopolitical instability in the Middle East and changes in freight rates as factors that could affect future results. The company operates in more than 90 countries and serves more than 300 ports worldwide.

**ZIM Price Action:** ZIM Integrated Shipping shares were up 4.11% at \$30.40 during premarket trading on Wednesday. The stock is trading near its 52-week high of \$30.96, [according to Benzinga Pro data](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3).

*Trump said after meeting Qatar’s prime minister on 9 November that the war is militarily “effectively over” and that new strikes are “quite unlikely,” while Tehran denied that a Vance–Rezaei meeting in Doha is planned and insisted the US first meet its seven conditions. Brent fell below $90 on 10 November for the first time since August as traders priced in restraint, even as Iran-linked tanker attacks, US strikes on Qeshm island and Houthi missile fire at Riyadh continued. France formally blamed the IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) for an October cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration, and the US moved aircraft off a second British base on an Iranian threat. A House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth over the war is due this week.*

Subscribe

## Military Operations & Ceasefire Status

- **US strikes on Qeshm island continue:** Iranian state media reported US strikes on Qeshm island overnight on 8–9 November; a provincial official told Fars they did not hit vital infrastructure or services, and the US did not comment. A senior Iranian source told Reuters the strikes targeted radar serving air defence and ship navigation, plus bases for missile launchers and mine-laying systems ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-meet-iran-war-mediator-qatar-no-imminent-deal-seen-end-war-2026-11-09)). The Iranian account is an uncorroborated claim.

- **Tanker-attack tally from Iranian state TV:** A state television reporter said on 9 November that 11 tankers had been “disabled” over the past 10 days; Iran typically does not acknowledge striking vessels. Reuters cited maritime-agency data showing attacks on Gulf and Hormuz tankers at the highest rate of the war ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-meet-iran-war-mediator-qatar-no-imminent-deal-seen-end-war-2026-11-09)).

- **US moves aircraft off a second UK base:** The Wall Street Journal reported that the US evacuated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall on 9 November after a threat from Iran, diverting refuelling tankers to Germany and raising RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the second-highest alert level. The precise threat is still under discussion among US officials, and the UK Ministry of Defence declined to comment on it ([SMH, citing WSJ](https://www.smh.com.au/world/north-america/us-aircraft-evacuated-from-second-british-base-due-to-iran-threat-report-20261110-p61d26.html)). Conway Analytics assesses this signals concern over Iranian-linked sabotage inside Europe rather than a conventional strike.

- **Trump: “locked and loaded” but holding:** Trump told Reuters the US is ready to resume strikes “anytime we want,” and told reporters that Iran is militarily “effectively over,” adding that the US is “just keeping it the status quo” ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/energy/gas-prices-fall-4-gallon-oil-markets-trump-iran-war-russia-ukraine-rcna608498); [Reuters via Jerusalem Post](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-914386)). No ceasefire exists; the naval blockade and Operation Iron Gate (the land-route restriction) remain in force.

## Diplomatic & Nuclear Developments

- **Qatar meeting yields “positive momentum,” no deal:** Trump met Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani on 9 November. # Oil prices rise after Trump says no Iran deal needed: 'We've got their Strait'

Published Thu, Nov 12 20268:24 AM ESTUpdated Thu, Nov 12 20267:01 PM EST

[Deena Zaidi](https://www.cnbc.com/deena-zaidi/)

![thumbnail](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/107148248-1667938600296-fred_IMG_3044.jpg?v=1667938658&w=60&h=60&ffmt=webp)

[Fred Imbert](https://www.cnbc.com/fred-imbert/)[@foimbert](https://twitter.com/foimbert)

Follow your favorite stocksCREATE FREE ACCOUNT

U.S. oil prices rose Thursday, as comments from President [Donald Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/donald-trump/) stoked worries that an end to the U.S.-Iran war was not in sight.

[Brent crude](/quotes/@LCO.1/) settled 3.3% higher at \$95.82 per barrel. [West Texas Intermediate futures](/quotes/@CL.1/) were up 2.6% to settle at \$88.74 per barrel.

"We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Trump [said in a Truth Social post](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/trump-iran-deal-hormuz-strait.html).

Jeffrey Currie, founder of Real Macro and a widely followed forecaster on Wall Street, said oil prices in the near term will remain tame because there is now a substantial amount of volume coming out of the Middle East. However, he noted that sky-high insurance and tanker rates are keeping prices elevated on longer-dated oil futures contracts.

"While it caps the prompt barrel, it does nothing to cheapen the next one, which is why you can't get bearish here nor can you get really bullish," said Currie to CNBC's ["The Exchange."](https://www.cnbc.com/the-exchange/)

On the investing front, Currie said he still favors long-dated oil and the drilling and producer stocks.

![hide content](https://static-redesign.cnbcfm.com/dist/a54b41835a8b60db28c2.svg)

Brent and WTI- YTD

Thursday's moves come as oil prices have been under pressure after comments from Trump following the U.S. midterm elections eased fears of further strikes on Iran. WTI is down 16% in November, and Brent has lost 20%.

Trump said Sunday that fresh attacks were [highly unlikely](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/oil-falls-as-trump-says-new-iran-attacks-unlikely.html) as talks to end the conflict progressed, despite both ⁠countries reporting that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. He also [said further military action did not appear](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/oil-falls-as-trump-downplays-prospect-of-escalation-with-iran.html) necessary "at this point," easing concerns about prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil supplies.

John Kilduff, a partner at Again Capital, said investors may have been too quick to price in an end to the fighting.

"The market may have gotten ahead of itself on pricing in a cessation of hostilities," Kilduff told CNBC. He warned that renewed doubts about a deal would push the security premium in oil prices higher.

Trump's assertion that the U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz could spur further Iranian attacks on shipping, increasing the risk of prolonged supply disruptions, according to Kilduff.

"The President may be thinking that given enough time, the economic blockade of Iran will force them to either negotiate with the USA or result in a regime change as the Iranian economy collapses. The Iranians might have different ideas and continue to attack Middle East Infrastructure that results in higher prices and forces the President to the negotiating table," said Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates.

"In any event, it does not seem to me that either side's negotiating position has changed. Iran wants the blockade to end, sanctions to be lifted and a ceasefire including Lebanon to be declared. The USA wants Iran to get rid of its entire nuclear stockpile and allow free transit through the Strait of Hormuz," he said.

*—CNBC's Pippa Stevens contributed to the report.*

passages.passage: Even through an uproar of violence in the 1980s when Iranian forces laid mines along the waterway, the Strait of Hormuz had never been closed. In March, the Iran war changed that reality in a break with tradition that energy analysts and strategists once looked at as an impossibility.

passages.under: The Strait of Hormuz was the biggest game changer for markets in 2026
passages.passage: The market effects from the Strait of Hormuz's closure were immediate. By the end of March, the price of the Brent (BZ=F) crude futures, the global benchmark crude oil contract, had reached a multiyear high of $118.35 per barrel as oil exports from the Persian Gulf evaporated. Prices on WTI crude (CL=F), the US equivalent contract, surged just as sharply.

passages.passage: - US inflation rose 0.4 per cent monthly in October, exceeding forecasts and reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. - About 90 per cent of traders expect the Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its final policy meeting of the year. - The Iran war continues to drive elevated energy and food costs, with maritime insurance and oil transfers raising crude prices by between $20 and $30 a barrel. - Treasury yields climbed sharply following the inflation report, with the 10-year benchmark returning to 5 per cent and the 30-year rising above 5.36 per cent. - "Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk; a risk I am not eager to take," Fed governor Christopher Waller said.

# First Solar Analysts Cut Their Forecasts After Q3 Earnings

**First Solar Inc** [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR)[FSLR](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR)) reported mixed results for the third [quarter on Thursday](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR/earnings-forecasts).

The company posted quarterly earnings of \$5.30 per share which beat the analyst consensus estimate of \$4.60 per share. The company reported quarterly sales of \$1.231 billion which missed the analyst consensus estimate of \$1.288 billion.

First Solar slashed its FY2026 sales guidance from \$4.900 billion-\$5.200 billion to \$4.600 billion-\$4.900 billion.

“Section 232 represents a structural change in how the United States approaches solar manufacturing,” said Mark Widmar, Chief Executive Officer, “As a technology company and the only fully-integrated utility-scale solar manufacturer without dependency on the Chinese crystalline silicon supply chain, we believe we are structurally positioned to benefit from this environment.”

First Solar shares fell 4.7% to \$168.50 in pre-market trading.

These analysts made changes to their price targets on First Solar following earnings announcement.

- Bernstein analyst Sunaina Ocalan maintained the stock with an Underperform rating and lowered the price target from \$197 to \$169.
- Needham analyst Sean Milligan maintained the stock with a Buy and lowered the price target from \$303 to \$236.
- Evercore ISI Group analyst Nicholas Amicucci maintained the stock with an In-Line rating and cut the price target from \$218 to \$189.

**Considering buying FSLR stock? Here’s what analysts think:**

[![](https://editorial-assets.benzinga.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/30085647/image-639-1024x284.png)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR/price-targets)

*Photo via Shutterstock*

# First Solar Jumps 9% After Democratic Sweep, but Trump’s Tariffs Already Favor It

**First Solar Inc.** [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR)[FSLR](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLR)) jumped as much as 9% in Wednesday’s premarket trading after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, raising hopes of renewed federal support for clean energy.

But the leading U.S. solar manufacturer already benefits from billions in manufacturing tax credits, while President **Donald Trump’s** import restrictions could strengthen its competitive position.

The rally extended across the sector, with **Sunrun Inc.** [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RUN)[RUN](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RUN)) and **Enphase Energy Inc.** [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ENPH)[ENPH](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ENPH)) also posting substantial premarket gains.

The question is how much additional help Democrats can deliver.

### What Democrats Could Change

First Solar already [expects](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1274494/000127449426000211/ex991pressreleaseq3-2026.htm) about \$2.1 billion in federal tax credits this year for manufacturing solar panels in the U.S. Those subsidies are protected at their full value through 2029.

But the customers buying those panels face a different situation.

Trump’s 2025 tax law eliminated key incentives for most new solar projects beginning operations after 2027, although projects that started construction by July 4, 2026, remain eligible.

Restoring those incentives could encourage developers to build more solar farms, boosting demand for First Solar’s panels.

There is one major obstacle: Trump can veto any attempt to restore the credits. Democrats won’t take control of Congress until January, and even then they lack the votes to override him.

[Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxvetooverride/veto-override/kxvetooverride-29jan20) traders assign a 28% probability that Congress will override at least one Trump veto before Jan. 1, 2028. The market has approximately \$108,000 in total trading volume.

The contract covers any presidential veto, not specifically clean-energy legislation, but illustrates the broader political hurdle facing Democrats.

### Trump’s Tariffs Could Help First Solar

While Democrats debate how to support solar energy, Trump’s tariffs are already giving First Solar an advantage over foreign competitors.

Starting Dec. 4, covered imported solar panels will [face](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/08/adjusting-imports-of-polysilicon-and-its-derivatives-into-the-united-states) a minimum price of 38 cents per watt, plus an additional 15% duty on many covered imports. That makes it harder for overseas manufacturers to undercut First Solar’s American-made panels.

CEO **Mark Widmar** said on First Solar’s Oct. 29 earnings [call](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/fslr/transcripts/720237-q3-2026/) that it had raised prices in some customer negotiations following the tariff announcement.

But there’s a catch.

Widmar said uncertainty over how the new import rules and other restrictions will be enforced has made it harder for customers to agree on prices, slowing new orders.

First Solar cut its annual sales forecast from \$4.9 billion–\$5.2 billion to \$4.6 billion–\$4.9 billion, citing weaker expected sales of panels manufactured in India and other overseas facilities, as well as U.S.-finished products.

That leaves First Solar in an unusual position: Trump’s tariffs have already helped it raise its asking prices, but uncertainty over the new rules is making it harder to turn those negotiations into firm orders.

# Homebuilders, Miners and Regional Banks Soar as Oil Drops 8%: Has the Hormuz Peace Trade Begun?

For eight months, the war in the Gulf had a clear set of [winners](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/commodities). On Monday, Wall Street started paying the losers instead.

Homebuilders, gold miners and regional banks led the market after Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington accepts its terms.

Oil went the other way. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 7.2% to \$96.63 a barrel by mid-afternoon in New York, while Brent dropped 7.6% to \$104.77.

The **State Street SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XHB)[XHB](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XHB)) climbed 3.3%, outpacing every major sector. The **VanEck Gold Miners ETF** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GDX)[GDX](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GDX)) rose 3.2% and the **State Street SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KRE)[KRE](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KRE)) gained 2.4%.

Travel stocks, among the biggest casualties of expensive fuel, rallied hard. The **U.S. Global Jets ETF** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/JETS)[JETS](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/JETS)) jumped 4.2%, the biggest gain among industry ETFs.

The **State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XLE)[XLE](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XLE)) sank 3.5%.

Is Wall Street pricing the end of the war, or just the hope of one?

## **Iran Cuts Its Hormuz Timeline From Seven Days to Two**

Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** said talks with Qatari mediators had produced a faster plan to reopen the waterway, according to a post on X by **The Middle East Letter**.

“On the first day, the U.S. implements a set of measures, and on the second day, the Strait of Hormuz reopens and transit returns to its previous state,” Araghchi said.

“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” foreign ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baqaei** said on Monday.

> BREAKING: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran and Washington have now reached what he described as a "two-day plan" for de-escalation.\
> \
> "On the first day, the U.S. implements a set of measures, and on the second day, the Strait of Hormuz reopens and transit…
>
> — The Middle East Letter (@themiddleeastle) [November 2, 2026](https://x.com/themiddleeastle/status/2117244456038445213?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The conditions are steep, from lifting the U.S. naval blockade to cutting American forces back to pre-war levels.

The stakes show up in the shipping data. Only five commodity vessels crossed the strait on Saturday and none on Sunday, compared with 31 the previous weekend, according to Kpler.

Gulf producers have found ways around the chokepoint. At least 16.5 million barrels a day of crude left the region in September, matching pre-war levels excluding Iran, but only 60% of it physically crossed Hormuz, Kpler data show.

**Read Also: [Refiner Stocks Suffer Worst Day Since the Tariff Shock: The Threat Is Not Cheaper Oil](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/10/62634697/refiner-stocks-valero-marathon-worst-day-since-april-2025-iran-russian-diesel)**

## **Why Homebuilders Lead the Peace Trade**

The link between Hormuz and the U.S. housing market runs through the bond market.

Higher oil lifted inflation, inflation lifted Treasury yields, and yields lifted mortgage rates, keeping buyers away.

The 10-year yield has risen about 95 basis points since the war began in late February. A credible end to the Hormuz disruption would reverse that chain.

Bonds rallied as oil fell. The 10-year yield dropped 3.7 basis points to 4.90%, the 30-year yield fell 3.8 basis points to 5.27% and the two-year yield slipped 1.3 basis points to 4.58%.

**PulteGroup Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PHM)[PHM](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PHM)) rose 5%, while **D.R. Horton Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DHI)[DHI](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DHI)) and **Lennar Corp.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LEN)[LEN](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LEN)) gained 4.3% each. Including **Toll Brothers Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TOL)[TOL](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TOL)), **NVR Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVR)[NVR](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVR)) and **KB Home** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KBH)[KBH](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KBH)), the six builders added about \$5.4 billion in market value.

## **Gold Fell During the War. It Rallies on Peace Hopes**

Gold was supposed to be the war hedge. Instead, bullion is down about 8.6% this year.

Gold pays no interest, so the same rise in yields that hurt homebuilders made it less attractive, as did a stronger dollar.

On Monday, both forces eased. Gold rose 1.9% to about \$3,948 an ounce and silver jumped 3.2% to \$50.69.

**Barrick Mining Corp.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/B)[B](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/B)) and **Newmont Corp.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NEM)[NEM](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NEM)) rose 3% each.

## **Regional Banks Bet on Less Fed Pressure**

The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4% last week, but two officials pushed for a hike, citing energy-driven inflation.

Cheaper oil weakens that argument, and fewer hikes would ease pressure on smaller banks’ deposit costs and borrowers.

**Western Alliance Bancorp.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WAL)[WAL](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WAL)) rose 3.5%.

**Read Also: [Trump Declares Iran War 'Terminated'. Hormuz Tells A Different Story](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/26/05/52233102/trump-iran-war-terminated-hormuz-blockade-oil-stocks)**

## **The Deal Is Not Done**

Washington has not accepted Iran’s terms. **President Donald Trump** rejected the original seven-day proposal, and Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** said over the weekend that no decision has been made.

Monday’s rotation is a bet on a deal, not a reaction to one. If talks stall, the same chain that lifted homebuilders, miners and regional banks could run in reverse.

*Image via Shutterstock*

# Novo Nordisk Raises 2026 Outlook As Wegovy Pill Shines

**Novo Nordisk A/S** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVO)[NVO](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVO)) stock rose Wednesday after the drugmaker reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its full-year outlook.

## Novo Nordisk’s Obesity Sales Jump 22%

The weight loss drugmaker reported third-quarter sales of \$11.90 billion (79.195 billion Danish kroner), beating Wall Street’s estimate of \$11.39 billion.

Sales rose 4% at constant exchange rates (CER), driven by strong demand for GLP-1 drugs, particularly obesity treatments.

Obesity [sales](https://www.novonordisk.com/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=919765) jumped 22% at CER to 26.146 billion kroner. Higher sales volumes across markets fueled the growth.

However, diabetes sales fell 5% at CER to 47.545 billion kroner.

U.S. GLP-1 diabetes sales declined 10% at CER due to lower volumes and changes in wholesaler inventories.

Injectable Ozempic sales fell 11% at CER, while oral semaglutide sales under the Rybelsus brand rose 5%.

Weekly new-to-brand prescriptions for the Ozempic pill are now about 100% higher than pre-launch levels under the Rybelsus brand.

## Novo Nordisk’s Operating Profit Jumps 27%

Adjusted operating profit climbed 27% at CER to 31.720 billion kroner.

GLP-1 sales growth and lower year-over-year transformation expenses supported profitability.

The company recorded about 9 billion kroner in transformation costs a year earlier. However, roughly 3.5 billion kroner in one-time expenses partly offset the latest quarter’s gains.

Novo Nordisk reported adjusted earnings of 87 cents per share (5.79 kroner), beating analysts’ [estimate of 81 cents](https://www.benzinga.com/earnings).

**See More: [Top Value Stocks](https://www.benzinga.com/screener/top-value-stocks)**

## Wegovy Pill Sets U.S. Launch Record

Wegovy pill prescriptions reached about 3.6 million during the quarter, bringing the total to more than 8 million since launch.

The company described it as the strongest GLP-1 volume launch in U.S. history.

The pill generated 4.178 billion kroner in U.S. sales during the quarter.

Meanwhile, injectable Wegovy [sales](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/8d56aec0-b469-4180-81ee-3c3c000beca2) reached 20.407 billion kroner, down 2% at CER.

Total Wegovy pill sales reached 5.394 billion kroner, while Ozempic sales fell 5% to 29.706 billion kroner.

Wegovy pill sales surged 53% from the previous quarter, beating the 4.62 billion kroner consensus estimate, Reuters reported.

CEO **Mike Doustdar** told Reuters that Novo has held its ground since Eli Lilly launched its rival pill. Investors said Novo leads in oral obesity treatments, while Lilly dominates the injectable market. However, they warned that competition could intensify.

## Novo Nordisk Raises 2026 Outlook

Novo Nordisk raised its 2026 forecast, citing stronger expectations [for GLP-1 sales](https://www.benzinga.com/calendars/guidance).

The company now expects adjusted sales growth and adjusted operating profit growth of negative 2% to positive 2% at CER.

Its previous forecast called for [declines of up to 6%](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/08/60924329/ozempic-maker-novo-nordisk-raises-outlook-but-sales-fall-on-tough-comparison-stock-tanks).

**NVO Price Action:** Novo Nordisk shares were up 6.64% at \$42.86 during premarket trading on Wednesday, [according to Benzinga Pro data](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3).

*Image via Shutterstock*

# Vistra Stock Soars After Surprising Q3 Sales Results

**Vistra Corp**. [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST)[VST](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST)) shares are popping Friday after reporting third-quarter sales that beat analyst estimates and raising the midpoint of its [2026 profit outlook](https://www.benzinga.com/node/62967183).

- Vistra stock is surging to new heights today. [What’s behind VST gains?](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST)

## Vistra Stock Rises After Third-Quarter Sales Beat

Vistra shares are climbing after the power producer beat Wall Street’s third-quarter sales forecast. Revenue hit roughly \$6.35 billion, topping the \$6.02 billion estimate by 5.36% and growing 27.68% from around \$4.97 billion in the same quarter last year. Adjusted EBITDA from ongoing operations soared more than 50% to \$2.378 billion.

Vistra also nudged up its 2026 profit guidance. It lifted the middle of its range while tightening it. Adjusted EBITDA from ongoing operations should land between \$7.1 billion and \$7.5 billion, and adjusted free cash flow before growth between \$4.3 billion and \$4.7 billion.

The company gave its first 2027 outlook as well: adjusted EBITDA from \$7.7 billion up to \$8.5 billion, an 11% jump at the midpoint, and free cash flow from \$4.3 billion up to \$5.1 billion. Price protections already cover about 98% of expected 2027 volumes and about 78% of 2028, on top of nearly all of 2026.

CEO **Jim Burke** credited a scorching summer, noting the fleet stayed reliable while July demand set records in the ERCOT and PJM power markets. Burke said that “we continue to be well positioned for the growing demand ahead.”

## Vistra Closes Cogentrix and Signs New Power Deals

Vistra completed its purchase of Cogentrix in October, adding about 5,500 megawatts of natural gas generation. Management said on the conference call that the deal should lift adjusted free cash flow by a high-single-digit percentage soon and by double digits from 2029.

Vistra also reported progress on new projects. It started running its 405-megawatt Pulaski Solar project in Illinois, which sells power to Microsoft, and its 100-megawatt Deer Creek solar and storage site in California. A two-decade deal now commits 207 megawatts from its Odessa gas plant in Texas to New Era Energy and Digital.

Executives said the midterm outcome leaves their view of Vistra’s growth opportunities unchanged. The company is negotiating with major electricity consumers across both the PJM and ERCOT markets, covering existing and new plants, and stays open to acquisitions that fit its fleet.

## VST Shares Are Surging

**VST Price Action:** [Vistra shares](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VST) were up 10.36% at \$124.59 at the time of publication on Friday, according to [Benzinga Pro](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3).

# D.R. Horton Warns of Continued Mortgage Pressure in Housing Demand

**D.R. Horton, Inc.** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DHI)[DHI](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DHI)) on Thursday reported mixed fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results, with earnings per share of \$2.67 missing the [\$3.03 analyst estimate](https://www.benzinga.com/pressreleases/26/10/b62686304/d-r-horton-inc-america-s-builder-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2026-earnings-and-increases-quart), while revenue of \$9.371 billion topped expectations of \$8.988 billion.

The homebuilder faced weaker demand and declining sales prices amid high mortgage rates and affordability pressures, while management warned of continued margin pressure in fiscal 2027.

**• D.R. Horton stock is trading in a tight range. [What’s the outlook for DHI shares?](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DHI)**

## **Home Sales and Demand Trends**

Homebuilding revenue fell 2% year-over-year to \$8.4 billion, while homes closed declined 2% to 22,915. The average closing price was \$365,600, 27% below the U.S. new-home average in the fourth quarter.

Net sales orders decreased 7% Y/Y to 18,619 homes, while order value fell [9% to \$6.6 billion](https://www.benzinga.com/earnings). The average order price declined 2% to \$356,600.

The cancellation rate rose to 23%, up from 20% a year earlier and in the previous quarter. Active selling communities increased 10% Y/Y.

Management cited high mortgage rates, affordability constraints and cautious consumer sentiment as factors weighing on demand.

## **Profitability and Cash Flow**

Home sales gross margin fell 120 basis points sequentially to 19.5%, pressured by weaker pricing power and litigation costs. Management expects continued margin pressure and elevated incentives in fiscal 2027.

D.R. Horton started 13,100 homes in the fourth quarter, down 10% Y/Y. Land and development investments totaled \$2 billion during the quarter, bringing the fiscal-year total to \$8.2 billion.

The company generated \$3.5 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2026 and ended Sept. 30 with \$7.2 billion in liquidity, including \$2.1 billion in cash and \$5.1 billion in available credit facilities.

## **Shareholder Returns**

D.R. Horton returned \$4.1 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2026 through share repurchases and dividends. Over the past five years, the company returned \$14 billion to shareholders.

The board increased the quarterly dividend by 11% to \$0.50 per share, marking 13 consecutive years of dividend-per-share growth.

**See More: [Top Growth Stocks](https://www.benzinga.com/screener/top-growth-stocks)**

## **Fiscal 2027 Outlook**

D.R. Horton expects first-quarter revenue of \$5.9 billion-\$6.4 billion, below the \$6.963 billion analyst estimate. For fiscal 2027, the company forecasts revenue of \$30 billion-\$32 billion, compared with the [\$33.653 billion estimate](https://www.benzinga.com/calendars/guidance).

The company expects fiscal 2027 home closings of 79,000-84,000, operating cash flow of approximately \$3.5 billion, \$3 billion in share repurchases and \$500 million in dividends.

passages.under: Novo Nordisk Buys Time: A 27% Profit Jump, a New CFO, and a Guidance Call Deferred to February
passages.passage: Novo Nordisk beat Q3 estimates and raised 2026 outlook, but deferred 2027 guidance and faces U.S. list-price cuts from January 1, 2027.

passages.under: Novo Nordisk Buys Time: A 27% Profit Jump, a New CFO, and a Guidance Call Deferred to February
passages.passage: Novo Nordisk delivered a third-quarter beat that sent its shares up 4.8% yesterday, but the more telling signal came from what management did not say. Chief executive Mike Doustdar declined to issue guidance for 2027, pushing that reckoning to the full-year results in February 2027. Between now and then, investors must decide whether the company's volume-led recovery can outrun the price cuts it has already scheduled for the U.S. market.

passages.under: The Price Test Arrives on January 1
passages.passage: Then there is the arithmetic of pricing. From January 1, 2027, Novo Nordisk will lower its U.S. list prices, with Ozempic expected to see an annual decline of 10–15%. More patients will therefore be needed simply to hold revenue steady, let alone grow it. The central question for the investment case is whether prescription volume can convert into revenue once those cuts take effect — a link the company has not yet made explicit.

passages.under: A New Finance Chief Alongside the Numbers
passages.passage: The first real stress test begins with the U.S. list-price reductions at the turn of the year. The 2027 forecast, due alongside the full-year figures in February, is where Novo Nordisk must finally connect the dots between more patients, lower prices and expected financial performance. Until that outlook lands, a rising prescription count alone will not settle the case — only guidance that holds up under pricing pressure will.

passages.passage: The acquisition agreement announced in February calls for Hapag-Lloyd of Germany to pay $35 per Zim (NYSE: ZIM) share in cash, valuing the Israeli carrier’s equity at approximately $4.2 billion. Zim shareholders have already approved the merger, but closing remains contingent on government and regulatory clearances, including consent tied to Israel’s “golden share.”

passages.under: $4.2B takeover in limbo
passages.passage: The deal also faces a governance issue. A shareholder group representing more than 10% of Zim’s shares has called for another shareholder vote if the revised arrangement is materially different from the transaction approved earlier this year. The group argues that board approval alone would be inadequate for a substantially altered deal structure, although reporting to date has not established that Israeli law or the merger agreement legally requires a second vote.

passages.under: $4.2B takeover in limbo
passages.passage: The distinction matters. Hapag-Lloyd and Zim can contend that the purchase price and merger agreement remain intact while the FIMI/New Zim carve-out is strengthened to satisfy the state. Dissenting shareholders may argue that changes to the assets, governance and state-share protections amount to a revised transaction deserving renewed investor approval.

# Hapag-Lloyd’s better ZIM offer runs into Israel’s clock

## The short version

Hapag-Lloyd adds ships to save ZIM deal, but time is the problem. Hapag-Lloyd has sweetened its $4.2 billion ZIM takeover for Israel: 16 ships for a new Israeli carrier instead of 11, plus a new Asia route. CEO Rolf Habben Jansen says the plan gives Israel “materially more maritime independence”. Our view: the terms are better, but the clock is worse. Israel’s state shareholder body stopped its review, so any new plan starts from zero. The Loadstar says the deal faces a February 2027 deadline to close. Forwarders should treat ZIM as a standalone carrier for 2027 contracts. We expect no Israeli approval before 31 December 2026.

**Hapag-Lloyd adds ships to save its ZIM deal, but Israel’s restarted review makes a 2026 close unlikely**

Hapag-Lloyd has put a better offer to Israel to save its $4.2 billion takeover of ZIM. The new Israeli company that would stay behind, Zim Israel, would get 16 ships instead of the 11 required under current rules, FreightWaves reports. It would also get a new weekly route to Asia. Hapag-Lloyd chief executive Rolf Habben Jansen set out the revised plan, drawn up with Israeli investment firm FIMI, in comments carried again by Container News this week.

Our view is simple. The terms are better. The clock is worse. Israel’s review has gone back to the start, and the deal has a closing deadline only months away. We think a 2026 close is now out of reach, and forwarders should plan for ZIM as an independent carrier well into 2027.

### **What is on the table**

The deal was announced in February. Hapag-Lloyd agreed to pay $35 per ZIM share in cash, about $4.2 billion in total, according to the announcement published by AJOT on 16 February. That price was a 58% premium to ZIM’s share price on 13 February.

The structure is unusual. Israel holds a “golden share” in ZIM. That is a special share that gives the state a veto over control of the company, because ZIM carries Israel’s cargo in wartime and emergencies. To get around it, Hapag-Lloyd would take ZIM’s international business. FIMI would set up a separate Israeli company to hold the assets the golden share protects, FreightWaves explained on 25 September.

The revised plan, first presented when Habben Jansen flew to Israel on 24 September, adds several things for that Israeli company. According to The Maritime Executive, Zim Israel would:

> - add a weekly Far East route alongside its planned Mediterranean and transatlantic services

> - double its reefer capacity (refrigerated containers for food and pharma)

> - keep vessel management and expertise in Israel, with its own IT system

> - sign a long-term commercial agreement with Hapag-Lloyd for global access

FreightWaves also reports that government scrutiny of foreign buyers in the Israeli company could start at a 10% stake rather than 24%. For workers, The Maritime Executive says the plan reportedly includes no layoffs through the end of 2027. The price has not changed. The Maritime Executive, citing Globes, says the valuation stays at $4.2 billion, or $35 a share.

Habben Jansen is confident. “The substantially improved proposal gives Israel materially more maritime independence,” he said, as quoted by Container News. He added: “We are confident that the strengthened proposal addresses the concerns raised.”

### **Why the clock matters more than the terms**

The problem is process, not price. Israel’s Government Companies Authority, which acts for the state’s golden share, stopped handling the original application. ZIM told the US Securities and Exchange Commission it had received a letter saying the file was closed because no revised proposal arrived by the set deadline, Seatrade Maritime reported on 1 October.

That means a fresh start. A materially revised structure needs a new application and a new review, Container News reported on 2 October. The Loadstar says the authority will not accept a resubmission until ZIM, FIMI and Hapag-Lloyd have all approved it. It adds that the earlier review had already taken six months.

Look at how long the first round took. The approval request went in during March 2026, Seatrade Maritime reports. In July, Israeli media reported that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz had raised national-security concerns at a cabinet meeting, Dow Jones reported. In September, Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI wrote to say they would submit revised proposals. By the end of that month the file was closed. The Loadstar reported that ZIM had been told any resubmission would need to be made by 6 October. About six months of review produced no decision.

Then there is the deadline. The Loadstar reports that a slow restart risks “the February 2027 deadline required to close the deal.” The Maritime Executive, citing Globes, says closing is now likely to slip from the end of 2026 to mid-2027. Those two reports point the same way. A six-month review, restarted in October, runs past February.

The paperwork is not even finished. The Maritime Executive reported on 24 September that full documentation was due within 45 days. Container News says details will go to Israeli authorities “over the coming weeks.” Habben Jansen argues that Israel’s objections “relate to our original proposal and do not take into account the significant improvements,” according to Container News on 2 October.

### **The opposition is political, and it is not done**

This is not a normal competition review. The objections are about national security.

The Times of Israel reports that Israel’s Defense Ministry concluded over the summer that the sale did not protect national security, especially in emergencies. Defense Minister Israel Katz backed that view. The paper also notes that Hapag-Lloyd’s shareholders include a subsidiary of Qatar’s sovereign wealth fund, with 12.3%, and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, with 10.2%. Seatrade Maritime lists those Gulf stakes among the main concerns.

Workers are against it too. ZIM union chief Oren Caspi told The Times of Israel that Israel should have at least 50 ships under its control. “With this revised proposal, Hapag-Lloyd prevents the government from making a decision,” he said. He also warned: “The uncertainty is already causing damage, as workers are leaving us in Israel and abroad.”

Some shareholders want a say again. A group holding more than 10% of ZIM’s shares wants another vote if the revised deal is materially different, FreightWaves reports. It notes that reporting so far does not show a second vote is legally required.

“Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI have listened carefully to the State of Israel,” Habben Jansen told The Times of Israel. In our reading, that is a buyer that knows it needs this approval.

### **The market has doubted this deal from the start**

Investors have never priced this as a sure thing. In early March, ZIM shares traded at $27.54, about $7.46 below the $35 offer, according to 24/7 Wall St. That gap is called the merger spread. A wide spread means investors doubt the deal will close. The article put it bluntly: “the market is pricing in the real possibility that this deal will never close.”

In July, ZIM shares fell about 5.7% to $24.11 after Israeli media reported that senior officials opposed the deal, Dow Jones reported. The shares have traded well below the offer price at both points we checked. That tells you how the money sees Israeli approval.

### **What it means for forwarders**

On the water, nothing changes yet. FreightWaves notes that Hapag-Lloyd and ZIM must operate independently until closing. So ZIM is still a separate carrier, setting its own prices and its own network.

That matters most on the transpacific. ZIM is a significant player on Asia–North America routes, including services via Vancouver and Prince Rupert, according to FreightWaves. Independent capacity there gives shippers an option outside the big alliances. If the deal slips to mid-2027, ZIM goes through next year’s annual contract talks as a standalone carrier.

Scale is the long-term issue. Container News reports the combined group would have more than 400 ships, over 3 million TEU (twenty-foot equivalent units, the standard container measure) of capacity, and handle more than 18 million TEU a year. Hapag-Lloyd puts annual synergies, the savings from combining, at up to €500 million. FreightWaves says Hapag-Lloyd’s own capacity would rise from 2.4 million to 3.1 million container units. That is not enough to lift it from fifth place on Alphaliner’s ranking into the top four. Hapag-Lloyd is part of the Gemini network, AJOT notes, so ZIM’s ships and lanes would eventually fold into that system.

For forwarders, our reading is:

> - **Contracts.** Do not assume ZIM pricing will move in line with Hapag-Lloyd in 2027. Negotiate them separately.

> - **Israel cargo.** If the deal closes, Israel trade would be served by a smaller Zim Israel plus Hapag-Lloyd. The new Asia route and doubled reefer capacity are promises in a proposal, not services yet.

> - **Staff and service.** Caspi’s warning that workers are leaving is worth watching. A long limbo can hurt service quality before any merger happens.

> - **Optionality.** Keep ZIM in routing guides as an alternative on transpacific and Mediterranean lanes while it remains independent.

### **Our call**

We think the revised terms improve the odds of Israeli approval, but not the timing. Our prediction: Israel will not approve the deal before 31 December 2026. By the end of February 2027, we expect Hapag-Lloyd and ZIM to extend the closing deadline rather than let the deal lapse, with closing pushed into mid-2027 at the earliest. If the Israeli review is still open at the end of the first quarter of 2027, the odds of the deal failing rise sharply, in our view.
